note: Layout migration, not content generation. Each fixture is a project at a different stack-it format; the skill must detect the format, restructure only the files the hop calls for, and leave every human-written byte alone. It never generates or refreshes stack content: the most it writes is the old CLAUDE.md text moved into docs/stack.md, inside the markers on the 1 to 2 hop and below the end marker when that file already exists, or a one-line stub when there was no block to move, so the AGENTS.md pointer always resolves. document-stack regenerates either one. The writes are ordered destination before source: docs/stack.md is written before the block is cut from CLAUDE.md. Fixtures for stop cases (broken-markers, invalid-lockfile) hold only the files that trigger the stop, since the checks halt the hop before any write.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-accept-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Two signals are readable and both say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md, so the highest signal is 1. All three checks run BEFORE any write: the lockfile validates, the CLAUDE.md markers are a clean single pair, and AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md resolve to ordinary separate files. Then the writes, in order: (a) stack.yaml gains 'format: 2' as the first top-level key with the rest of the file (key order, stack list order, notes, caveats) unchanged, and revalidates. (b) The block's text is CARRIED into docs/stack.md even though the lockfile exists and validated: a lockfile has fields for tools, versions, install steps, caveats and the provenance of the install steps, and none for operational notes, so anything else the block said lives nowhere else. The file is the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, then one <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair whose first line is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' followed by the carried content. Exactly one 'Generated by' line in the file, no old markers inside the carried text, and carried headings promoted one level ('## Tech Stack' becomes '# Tech Stack', '### Commands' becomes '## Commands'). (c) ONLY THEN is the whole marker block removed from CLAUDE.md, along with one surrounding blank line, leaving no double blank; the House rules and Deployment notes sections survive byte for byte. Cutting before the destination exists is a failure even when the end state looks the same. (d) AGENTS.md is created containing exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', with the path NOT in backticks and no HTML markers, and it resolves, because docs/stack.md now exists. (e) CLAUDE.md still has human prose, so the skill asks once and, on this yes, adds the single line '@AGENTS.md' at the top and nothing else. (f) README.md is untouched, markers and all. No stack content is generated anywhere, so the report says docs/stack.md holds the carried text and that document-stack runs next to regenerate it, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Dropping the block because a lockfile exists is the failure this pins.

evals.name: v1-with-lockfile-decline-import
evals.prompt: My stack-it files are in the old format. Bring them up to date with the new layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is no. Then run it once more. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Same detection, same three checks before any write, and the same write order as the accept case, including the block carried into docs/stack.md inside the markers under the 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' line before anything is cut from CLAUDE.md, except the bridge: the user declines the '@AGENTS.md' import, so the skill appends the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' to CLAUDE.md instead, with no markers, no '@AGENTS.md' line, and a blank line before it. Claude Code still reaches docs/stack.md, one hop instead of two, and the file it points at exists. The report lists CLAUDE.md under what CHANGED, not under what was left alone, says docs/stack.md holds the carried text and that document-stack runs next, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. The second run reads format 2 off the docs/stack.md header, verifies the layout, finds every piece in place, and changes nothing: it must not re-ask about the import, must not append a second pointer line, and must leave the already-present docs/stack.md byte for byte. It should also say the section is still a migrate placeholder and that document-stack has not filled it in.

evals.name: v1-no-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Only one signal is readable, the CLAUDE.md start marker, so the format is 1. There is no docs/stack.md and no .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml. With no lockfile the removed block is the only record of the (inferred) stack, and it is carried the same way it would be with one. docs/stack.md ends up as the header line '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, then a single <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair whose first line inside the start marker is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.', a blank line, then the carried content. Exactly one 'Generated by' line in the file: the block's own banner is dropped with the markers. No old stack-it markers survive inside the carried text. Carried headings are promoted one level ('## Tech Stack' becomes '# Tech Stack', '### Commands' becomes '## Commands'). Nothing is written below the end marker; the tail is document-stack's to fill when it carries notes forward. The report calls it a placeholder that document-stack will regenerate. That file is written BEFORE the block is cut. CLAUDE.md then keeps House rules and Deployment notes verbatim with the block and one blank line gone, and since the user said yes it also starts with the single line '@AGENTS.md'; AGENTS.md is created with the single pointer line; no lockfile is created or stamped (the skill must not fabricate a stack.yaml, and there is nothing to stamp); README.md is untouched. The report ends with 'migrated to 2'.

evals.name: already-current
evals.prompt: Can you migrate my stack-it artifacts to the latest layout? The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Detects format 2 from the docs/stack.md header, then verifies the layout is actually complete: no marker block in CLAUDE.md, docs/stack.md present with one clean marker pair, the pointer present in AGENTS.md, the bridge present, the format stamp present in stack.yaml. All of it holds, so it reports the project is current and changes NOTHING: no duplicate pointer line appended to AGENTS.md (it already contains @docs/stack.md, plus human-written house rules and deployment notes that stay verbatim), no edit to the one-line @AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md, no rewrite of docs/stack.md, no second 'format: 2' key in stack.yaml, no touching the README block. The '## Team notes' tail below the end marker in docs/stack.md is untouched, and so is the generated section: this skill never rewrites either, current or not. The section holds real content rather than a migrate line, so there is nothing to flag about document-stack not having run. Says what it checked and that there was nothing to do; a no-op run must be safe and obviously a no-op. The report ends with the line 'migrated to 2' verbatim, so a caller can parse the outcome.

evals.name: v1-block-only
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md is nothing but the marker block: there is no human prose to preserve. The lockfile exists and validates, and the block's text is still carried into docs/stack.md: header line, then one marker pair whose first line is 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.', then the carried content with its headings promoted one level and its own banner dropped. Only then does the cut run, and after it CLAUDE.md holds nothing but whitespace, so the bridge case 'doesn't exist, or holds nothing but whitespace' matches and the skill writes the single line '@AGENTS.md' WITHOUT asking. CLAUDE.md ends as exactly '@AGENTS.md' and nothing else. AGENTS.md is created with the pointer line and resolves, stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2', the README is untouched, and the report says docs/stack.md holds the carried text and that document-stack runs next before ending with 'migrated to 2'. Two failures this pins: asking the user about the bridge here, and dropping the block because a lockfile exists.

evals.name: broken-markers
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md has a '<!-- stack-it:stack start -->' with NO matching end marker, so where the generated block stops is unknowable. The format still reads 1 from the lockfile's missing key and from the marker itself, but marker integrity is check 2 and it fails, so the skill stops BEFORE the first write. Nothing at all changed: no text cut from CLAUDE.md, no format stamp on stack.yaml (the stamp is the first write and never runs), no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It shows the user the offending lines and ends with 'stopped: <reason>'. Two failures this pins: guessing the end of the block or deleting to end of file, and leaving a half-migrated tree because a check ran after a write.

evals.name: invalid-lockfile
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Check 1 runs before any write and fails with three problems: stack[0].version is the unquoted float 3.14, stack[1].install is an empty list, stack[2].choice is missing. The skill reports the validator's output verbatim and stops with NO edits: the CLAUDE.md block stays, no format stamp on stack.yaml, no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md, no bridge. It must not fix the lockfile, and it must not treat the failure as 'no usable lockfile' and run the hop around it: a lockfile that merely needs repair is not permission to restructure the project. Ends with 'stopped: <reason>'.

evals.name: unstamped-no-block
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile has no format key and there is nothing else to read: no docs/stack.md, no CLAUDE.md at all, so no marker block. A missing key reads as 1, which is behind, so the hop runs. This is a project that ran decide-stack on an older stack-it and never document-stack. Check 1 passes (the lockfile validates), check 2 finds no markers, which is not a failure but simply no block to cut, and check 3 has no symlinks to resolve. Writes: stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2' as the first top-level key and revalidates; with nothing to carry, docs/stack.md is written as the header line '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, and one <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair holding the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' (not the 'Moved from CLAUDE.md' line, since nothing moved); the cut is skipped; AGENTS.md is created with the single pointer line, which resolves; CLAUDE.md does not exist, so the bridge case creates it containing exactly '@AGENTS.md', with no ask. README.md is untouched. The report says docs/stack.md holds a stub and that document-stack runs next to fill it in, and ends with 'migrated to 2'. Leaving no docs/stack.md at all, so the fresh pointer aims at a missing file, is the half-state this pins.

evals.name: v2-leftover-block
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile is stamped 'format: 2' and docs/stack.md carries the format 2 header, so the project is already on the current layout; but CLAUDE.md still holds a '<!-- stack-it:stack start/end -->' block, left behind by a migration that did not finish. Layout verification catches it. The block's text must NOT go inside the markers of docs/stack.md: that section belongs to document-stack and is regenerated on every run, so anything written there is lost on the next pass. Instead, subject to marker integrity on both files, its content is appended BELOW the end marker under a '## Notes carried forward' heading, preceded by the single provenance line 'Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.' Same hygiene as the 1 to 2 hop: the block's own '> Generated by stack-it's document-stack' banner dropped, headings promoted one level, no old markers inside the carried text. The '### Gotchas' note about uv rebuilding the venv after a pyproject edit is the line that matters; it exists in no lockfile field. The tail already holds a '## Notes carried forward' heading, its provenance line, and one earlier note about DATABASE_URL: heading and line are reused, never doubled, the earlier note stays where it is, and the uv gotcha is appended after it. Block lines the section already states (Python 3.14.3, FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, the 'uv run pytest' command) are set aside and never appended, so the provenance line stays true. Only after that write does the block come out of CLAUDE.md, leaving the file as exactly '@AGENTS.md'. The generated section between the markers is byte for byte what it was, AGENTS.md and stack.yaml are untouched, no second 'format: 2' key appears, and the report names the repair it re-ran and lists what it carried. Two failures this pins: writing into the managed section, and cutting the block without carrying it because the lockfile could regenerate the tools.

evals.name: stamped-lockfile-only
evals.prompt: Migrate this project's stack-it files to the current layout. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The only file present is .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml, stamped 'format: 2'. There is no docs/stack.md, no AGENTS.md and no CLAUDE.md, all three, which is not a broken layout: this project was decided and locked but never documented. So there is nothing to repair and nothing to migrate. The skill changes NOTHING: it does not write a stub docs/stack.md, does not create the pointer, does not create the bridge, does not restamp the lockfile. It says the layout is current for what exists, that the project has not been documented yet, and that document-stack is the skill to run next, which will write all three files itself. Writing a stub and a pointer here is the failure this pins: migrate would be inventing a documentation stage the user never reached.
